title: How a septic tank works
caption: Where it ALL goes when you're not on a sewer 🚽 #howitworks #septic #homeowner #howitsbuilt #learnontiktok

lines.text: If your house isn't on a city sewer, every time you *flush*, it goes into your backyard.
You could just pipe it into a hole.
But raw sewage soaks into the ground and poisons the *well* water.
So you bury a big concrete *tank* instead.
Everything from the house flows in and sits still.
Heavy solids sink to the bottom and turn into *sludge*.
Grease floats to the top as *scum*.
And in the middle is mostly clear liquid.
Bacteria in the tank slowly eat away at the solids.
But a family fills a tank like this in just a few days.
So you add an outlet pipe in the middle layer, with a *baffle* so the scum can't escape.
That liquid flows out to a *drain field*: pipes full of holes, laid in trenches of gravel.
It trickles down through the soil, and the soil filters out the germs before it reaches the groundwater.
Which is why the grass over a drain field often grows the greenest in the yard.
But the sludge never fully goes away.
So every three to five years, a truck shows up and pumps it all out.
Congratulations, you just built a *septic system*.
